newsitem.title: UK: Gartman hates US bonds, likes Japan,baffled by EMU.
newsitem.headline: Gartman hates US bonds, likes Japan,baffled by EMU.

text.p: Financial markets watcher Dennis Gartman said on Thursday he was bearish on U.S. Treasuries, bullish on Japanese stocks, and completely befuddled by European currency union.

Gartman, an economist who edits The Gartman Letter out of the U.S., said the U.S. government and most of Wall Street have significantly underestimated the strength of the U.S. economy as its base shifts to the service sectors from manufacturing.
"The government still believes that Bethlehem Steel is what the U.S. produces," he told a seminar in London. "Services are what the U.S. produces."

"The economy of the U.S. is preposterously stronger than any of us believe it to be.... It means that demand for money is going to be greater and greater," he said. "I expect interest rates to be consistently higher," Gartman said.
He said the nonfarm payrolls report was probably the least important economic figure that he watches because it was so erratic.
He preferred to pay attention to tax revenues because they reflected true output.
Despite his view on the U.S. economy, he said he was no longer bullish on the dollar/yen rate. "The world is making the wrong bet on the Japanese economy."
He expected Japan's economy to rebound, prodded by financial reforms.
"I am phenomenally bullish on Japanese stocks," he said.

However, the recent events in Europe over European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) have left him perplexed. The row over German gold valuations has shown German Chancellor Helmut Kohl would do almost anything to get EMU on track.
He said France was unlikely to meet the three percent deficit to GDP ratio, and that meant EMU would be "fluffy at the edges" and that the euro launch would be delayed from the 1999 start date.

"I don't know what to do with it. I can make the fundamental case that I want to buy German marks. I can make the fundamental case that I want to sell German marks. And I can make the fundamental case that I want to leave German marks alone," he said.
